articles.description: Abstract Expansion Microscopy (ExM) enables nanoscale imaging of biological samples while preserving structural and molecular details. The Robust Non-rigid Registration Challenge for ExM (RnR-ExM) was launched to benchmark 3D registration algorithms on real-world ExM datasets. The challenge released 24 pairs of high-resolution 3D volumes from zebrafish, mouse, and C. elegans , deliberately selected for their difficulty with standard alignment methods. To evaluate performance, we provided curated segmentation masks of nuclei and blood vessels as landmarks for half of the dataset. To encourage learning-based approaches, we released code for generating synthetic training data reflecting the deformation and appearance of the unlabeled pairs. articles.description: Abstract Single-cell foundation models have transformed transcriptomic analysis, yet most rely on fixed gene identifiers that limit transfer across species and data types.
